audience_note: The Volta Basin evacuation displaced about 80,000 people; the Daedalus essay calls the evacuation of Worobong in October 1964 traumatic and chaotic, and says many settlers could not finish their one-room core houses.
title: Akosombo Dam, Volta River
summary: Akosombo Dam on the Volta River in Ghana was built between 1961 and 1965 by the Volta River Authority as part of the Volta River Project. The dam was closed in May 1964. Filling the reservoir displaced about eighty thousand people, and by 1963 the Volta River Authority had begun building fifty-two resettlement townships for people from 739 villages.

uncertainty.note: The Volta River Authority gives 1961 to 1965 for construction; Daedalus says construction began in 1961, the dam was closed in May 1964 and completed in 1965. End is the present: the dam operates.

as_recorded.value: Dam construction began in 1961; completed in 1965; With the closure of the Akosombo Dam in May 1964

reviewer_note: The VRA page contradicts itself on height (111 m at the axis, 141 m in text, 375 ft in the table), and on crest length (660 m vs 640 m). I record 111 m and 660 m, labelled. The 80,000 figure is rounded ("about eighty thousand"); earlier planning estimates (18,000; 62,000) differ.
